This integration shows in Gladys the Wolf heating system connected to an
**ISM8i** (or ISM8) module: gas and oil boilers, heat pumps, direct and mixer
circuits, cascade module, solar module, CWL ventilation, BM-2 control unit.
Everything stays on your local network, without any cloud nor Wolf account.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Wolf. **Never tested with a real
ISM8i**: it follows the ISM8 interface description published by Wolf and the
wolf_ism8 library (MIT) of the Home Assistant integration. Your feedback with
a real module is welcome.

## What you get

One Gladys device per Wolf element the ISM8i reports, with one feature per
value received:

- temperatures (boiler, flow, return, hot water, outdoor, flue gas, solar
  collector, room...), in °C;
- power of the heat pumps and of the solar module, in kW;
- states (burner, pumps, valves, fault, outputs), read only;
- operating states and programs as texts (never published as a measure 0),
  the last fault code;
- the system pressure, in Pa (the unit of the Wolf interface);
- percentages (burner, modulation, ventilation), setpoint corrections (K) and
  flows (l/h) as plain values, the unit in the name;
- the hot water setpoint and the heating and hot water programs of the direct
  circuit and of the mixer circuits 1 to 3, which can be changed (see below).

A device shows in the **Discovery** tab once the ISM8i sent one of its values.
Not shown in this version: dates and times, the energy counters of the solar
module, the air flows of the ventilation, the detection bit fields of the
BM-2.

## How the ISM8i reaches Gladys

The ISM8i opens the connection (TCP) itself, towards the server typed in its
web page; Gladys does not poll the module. So the integration starts a small
receiver next to it (the `ism8-link` container), whose port Gladys publishes
on the machine.

1. Give the ISM8i a fixed IP address in your router.
2. In the **Configuration** screen of the integration, type that address and
   save. **Nothing listens before**: the receiver starts only once a valid
   address is saved, and stops if you clear it.
3. Reload the screen: the "How the ISM8i reaches Gladys" section shows the
   port Gladys chose (a free port, kept afterwards). The ISM8i uses 12004 by
   default: replace it with this port.
4. In the web page of the ISM8i, set the server address to the IP address of
   the Gladys machine on your network, and this port.
5. The status of the integration turns to "ISM8i connected" at the first
   connection; the ISM8i then sends every value by itself.

### The network: what was checked

The Gladys core runs on the **host network** of the machine
(`network_mode: host`), but integrations run in isolated containers, on a
private Docker network: they cannot listen on the machine themselves. The
`ism8-link` receiver is a sub-container declared in the manifest, whose TCP
port 12004 Gladys publishes on **every address of the machine**
(`0.0.0.0:<chosen port>`). The ISM8i therefore reaches
`<IP address of the Gladys machine>:<port shown>`.

Checked in a test Gladys running in Docker (2026-10-28): nothing listens
before the address is saved; once saved, the port is published, a
connection from another address of the network arrives with **its real
source address** (Docker keeps it for traffic coming from the network) and
gets its acknowledgement; a connection
started on the Gladys machine itself arrives with the address of the Docker
gateway instead.

Hence:

- if your machine has a firewall, allow this TCP port;
- the **Check the sender** option (on by default) accepts only the address
  of the ISM8i; another address is refused before any byte is read, and the
  status shows the address seen. With Docker Desktop (Mac, Windows) or
  rootless Docker, Docker may replace the source address: the status then shows
  connections refused from an internal address; turn the option off in that
  case only: any machine of the network can then take the place of the
  ISM8i (the ISM8i is disconnected), send false values, receive the writes
  meant for the boiler, stops included, and confirm or contradict them;
- through Gladys Plus or a proxy, the address your browser shows is not the
  one the ISM8i must reach: use the local address of the machine.
- the receiver is started again only when it stopped or when the address
  or the sender check changes (each start drops the connection of the
  ISM8i). When the integration itself restarts (update, Gladys restart),
  Gladys restarts the receiver too: the ISM8i reconnects by itself, and the
  integration found the receiver again within 20 to 50 s in the test (the
  time Docker takes to forget the old container), up to about a minute.

## Changing settings

Off by default. With **Allow changing the settings**:

- **hot water setpoint**: whole degrees, from 20 °C to the hot water ceiling
  (65 °C by default, adjustable from 20 to 65 °C, never above 65 °C whatever
  is typed); a value above is refused, and the ceiling is checked again
  right before sending;
- **heating program**: automatic, heating (comfort), eco, standby;
- **hot water program**: automatic, continuous, standby.

A command leaves only if the option is on when it arrives **and** right
before sending, if the ISM8i is connected, and if the current value was
received during its current connection. It is said applied only when the
ISM8i reports the new value back (it reports every change by itself, and
every value is asked again about 5 s after the write, one request for
several writes); otherwise "sent, without confirmation". The outcome shows
in the status of the integration.

Never written: power and temperature presets of the boilers, time programs,
the one-off hot water charge, ventilation, and any other value.

### The stop (standby program) is never blocked

Choosing **Standby** (off, the frost protection of the Wolf controller
staying active) for the heating or the hot water of a circuit is always accepted:
option off, ceiling, value not read yet, another command running,
configuration not yet read from Gladys, nothing holds it. It is kept in
`/data` and:

- leaves at once when the ISM8i is connected, never held by the limits of
  the receiver (they do not apply to it);
- otherwise leaves at the next connection of the ISM8i, without waiting for
  the configuration (after a restart of the integration too, as soon as the
  ISM8i is back on the receiver);
- is confirmed by a value read: the ISM8i reports it, and every value is
  asked again once its 20 s of quiet are over;
- is sent again when nothing confirmed it 35 s after sending (3 s when it
  left less than 10 s after a request for every value), or 5 s apart when a
  value read contradicts it, 3 sendings at most in all; beyond that, the
  status asks you to check the boiler.

The only cases where it does not leave at once: the ISM8i is not connected,
its connection changed at that very moment (the stop then leaves at once on
the new one), the receiver is not running (address not saved yet), or the
receiver runs but does not answer the integration (it is then started again
after 3 minutes, at most every 10 minutes). It then waits in `/data` and the status says "stop kept", never "sent". No
"request all" is sent within 20 s of a stop not yet confirmed. Once
confirmed it is never sent again: a program changed later on
the boiler or in the Wolf app, read twice in a row, lifts the stop without
being fought. Choosing another program in Gladys (option on) lifts it too.
Time alone never lifts it.

While a stop of a circuit is not confirmed, every other change of that
circuit is refused (its hot water setpoint, its other program); choosing
another program for the stopped one stays allowed (it lifts the stop).

## Security

- The ISM8 protocol has **no password** and travels in clear: keep the ISM8i
  and Gladys on a trusted network.
- The receiver accepts 4 connections at most, one ISM8 session at a time (a
  new connection of the ISM8i replaces the old one), frames of 2048 bytes and
  300 values at most, checked whole; a malformed frame, a frame incomplete
  for 5 s or a flood of more than 1000 frames in 10 s closes the connection
  (a full dump is about 300); a value of 0 or more than 4 bytes is skipped.
- The receiver writes to the ISM8i only the hot water setpoints (20 to
  65 °C) and the program codes offered here, whatever it is asked.
- The channel between the receiver and the integration goes through the
  private network of the integration, with a mutual proof of a secret the
  integration generates.

## The "Read every value again" button

Asks the connected ISM8i to send every value again (at most every 30 s,
never within 20 s of a stop not yet confirmed). The integration also asks
when Gladys reconnects (fresh values), after writes and stops (grouped, see
above) and when a new connection brought no value within 2 s; otherwise the
ISM8i sends every value when it connects and each change afterwards.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Waiting for the ISM8i"**: check the server address and the port in the
  page of the ISM8i, the firewall of the Gladys machine, and that the ISM8i
  is on the same network.
- **"connection(s) refused from ..."**: the address seen is not the one
  typed; fix the address, or see above (Docker hiding the address).
- **A value is missing**: the ISM8i only sends what your installation has; a
  value outside its plausible range is never published.
- **Odd pressure**: the pressure is published in Pa as the Wolf interface
  says; tell us if a real module sends bar instead.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Wolf ISM8 asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Wolf heating, through its ISM8i module | `section` | No | Temperatures, states, faults and programs of the Wolf boilers, heat pumps, circuits and ventilation the ISM8i (or ISM8) module reports, on your local network, without any cloud. The ISM8i connects to Gladys by itself. Give it a fixed IP address in your router. Never tested with a real ISM8i. Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Wolf. |
| Address of the ISM8i | `string` | Yes | The IP address of the ISM8i module (the one of its web page), without a port. Nothing listens before it is saved. |
| How the ISM8i reaches Gladys | `section` | No | The ISM8i opens the connection itself. In its web page, set the server address to the IP address of the Gladys machine on your network and the port to \{\{port:ism8\}\} (chosen by Gladys, replacing the 12004 of the ISM8i). The port exists once the address of the ISM8i is saved: save, then reload this screen. Allow this port in the firewall of the Gladys machine if it has one. |
| Check the sender | `boolean` | No | Accept the connection only from the address of the ISM8i. Turn it off only if the status says connections come from another address because Docker hides the real one on this machine: then any machine of your network can take the place of the ISM8i, send false values, receive the writes meant for the boiler (stops included) and confirm or contradict them. |
| Changing settings | `section` | No | The hot water setpoint and the heating and hot water programs of the direct circuit and of the mixer circuits can be changed from Gladys once allowed below (off by default). The standby program (off, frost protection kept) is always allowed: stopping is never blocked. The ISM8 protocol has no password: keep it on a trusted network. |
| Allow changing the settings | `boolean` | No | Off: only the standby program can be selected; any other change is refused. |
| Hot water ceiling (°C) | `number` | No | A hot water setpoint above it is refused. 20 to 65 °C; never above 65 °C, whatever is typed. |
| Language of the names and messages | `select` | No |  |

## How to install Wolf ISM8 in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Wolf ISM8 appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-wolf-ism8:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-wolf-ism8](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-wolf-ism8).

Wolf ISM8 requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Wolf ISM8 is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
